2607.08409.title: When Synthetic Speech Is All You Have: Better Call GRPO
2607.08409.paper_summary: LLM-based ASR adapted to regulated domains such as banking is bottlenecked by privacy: real speech is costly and legally constrained to collect, making synthetic text-to-speech (TTS) an attractive substitute. Yet synthetic speech stays acoustically mismatched with real recordings, and work on this gap has stayed within supervised fine-tuning (SFT). We instead turn to reinforcement learning, and show that Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) extracts far more from the same synthetic speech than SFT. Synthetic-only adaptation of the model with GRPO, a critic-free method rewarding low-WER hypotheses, reduces WER by 40\% relative to SFT (36.71\%$\to$22.09\%), and an SFT-then-GRPO combination pushes this further to 45\%. We trace the gain to behavior rather than representation: GRPO reduces insertion errors by improving stopping calibration and speech-to-text alignment by better anchoring attention to audio, leaving early-layer representations intact. When synthetic speech is the main resource, reinforcement learning should be preferred over supervised fine-tuning.
2607.08409.paper_summary_zh: LLM 基於 ASR 的系統在受管制的領域如銀行業受到隱私的瓶頸：實際語音的收集成本高且受到法律限制，使得合成的文本轉語音（TTS）成為一個有吸引力的替代方案。<lb/>然而，合成語音在聲學上與真實錄音存在不匹配的情況，而對於這一差距的研究仍然停留在監督式微調（SFT）之內。<lb/>我們則轉向強化學習，並展示群體相對策略優化（GRPO）從相同的合成語音中提取的資訊遠超過 SFT。<lb/>使用 GRPO 對模型進行僅合成的適應，這是一種不需要評估者的方法，通過獎勵低 WER 假設，將 WER 相對於 SFT 降低了 40\%（36.71\%$\to$22.09\%），而 SFT 然後 GRPO 的組合進一步將其推高至 45\%。<lb/>我們將這一增益歸因於行為而非表徵：GRPO 通過改善停止校準和語音到文本的對齊來減少插入錯誤，通過更好地將注意力固定於音頻上，保持早期層的表徵不變。<lb/>當合成語音是主要資源時，應優先考慮強化學習而非監督式微調。
